title: Instant coffee: your on-the-go sidekick
summary: Get exact functional instant coffee ratios and water temperature for a smooth, bitter-free cup, plus methods, iced and americano variations, and storage.
body_markdown:
Instant coffee gives you a full cup in about a minute, with no brewer and no filter required. Early meetings, long flights, cold mornings at the trailhead: your day doesn't always wait for a brew, but instant coffee is there to make sure you get one anyway.


Here's the basic method for a typical jar of instant coffee granules: Use about 1 teaspoon per 6 oz of water, or up to 2 teaspoons for an 8 oz or stronger cup. Heat the water to about 80 to 85°C (175 to 185°F), just off the boil. Spoon the granules into your mug, add a splash of water and stir to a paste. Top up and stir until no specks remain.

**Cinnamon.** It brings a warm, familiar spice that feels right in the cooler months. The flavor profile reads as sweet and tames the sharpness of coffee.


**A pinch of salt.** This hack has been found to quiet bitter compounds in foods and drinks.


### Beyond the basic brew: iced, latte, coconut water americano and smoothie


Your Functional Instant Coffee dissolves in hot or cold water, so you're ready for any recipe below with[PERFORM](https://lairdsuperfood.com/products/perform-coffee-instant?variant=43976388149283) ,[FOCUS](https://lairdsuperfood.com/products/focus-instant-coffee?variant=43977767485475) ,[DIGEST](https://lairdsuperfood.com/products/digest-instant-coffee?variant=43977757229091) or[Mushroom](https://lairdsuperfood.com/products/mushroom-instant-coffee?variant=44049994612771) .


- **Shaken espresso.** Stir one serving into 2-4 oz of cold water in a jar, add a generous handful of ice, shake vigorously until frothed, then pour into a glass.
- **Latte.** Dissolve one serving of instant coffee in 2-4 oz of hot water. Top it with steamed or frothed milk. For a dairy-free option, dissolve a generous serving of Superfood Creamer in a little more hot water, use a frother to blend and lighten it, then pour it over your hot instant coffee.
- **Coconut water americano.** Stir one serving of Functional Instant Coffee and one Hydrate stick pack into 4 oz of cold water, then pour over ice. Hydrate is made with coconut water and Aquamin, a bioactive, multi-mineral complex and a source of natural electrolytes. Perfect for after a ride or a hike.
- **Coffee smoothie.** Blend one serving or stick pack with a banana, dates, cacao powder, milk of choice, and ice for a delicious mocha smoothie.


### Troubleshooting


Most hiccups with your Functional Instant Coffees come down to moisture, water, or dose.


**Granules won't dissolve:** Make a paste first with a splash of hot water. Then stir until the bottom is clear. If your bag has hardened into clumps, moisture got in. Instant coffee starts caking at around 5 to 7% moisture. Keep your bag sealed in a cool, dry spot.


**Too bitter.** Try a pinch of salt or a splash of Superfood Creamer. If your tap water is hard or smells of chlorine, use soft, filtered water.


**Too weak.** Use the 8 oz end of the 8 to 10 oz range.


### FAQ


**Is instant coffee just finely ground coffee?**


No, instant coffee is brewed coffee with the water taken out, keeping only what dissolved. Factories brew roasted coffee, concentrate it, then freeze-dry or spray-dry it to under 5% moisture. Grounds won't fully dissolve, thanks to cellulose, a tough plant fiber water can't break down. Our Functional Instant Coffees start from organic, freeze-dried arabica, so stir a serving into cold water and watch it disappear.


**Can you make instant coffee in a coffee machine?**


Keep the granules out of the brew basket and pod holder, since they dissolve on contact and leave nothing to brew. Instead, use the machine as a hot water source, since many espresso machines have a hot-water outlet. On a pod brewer, run a cycle with no pod into your mug. Then stir in your instant coffee.


**Should I use boiling water for instant coffee?**


Major instant coffee makers recommend water just off the boil, about 80 to 85°C (175 to 185°F). If your kettle has no temperature setting, let it rest off the base for a bit after it comes to a boil, then pour.


**How much caffeine is in instant coffee?**


PERFORM, FOCUS, and DIGEST Instant Coffees each have 70 mg of caffeine per serving. Mushroom Instant Coffee has 45 mg per serving. For context, an 8 oz cup of brewed coffee averages about 95 mg. The FDA cites 400 mg a day as safe for most healthy adults. That's an amount not generally linked to negative effects.


**Does instant coffee expire?**


Instant coffee is shelf stable, but it does lose quality over time. At room temperature, most jars and tins remain fresh at 1 year unopened and 2 to 3 months opened. To store an opened bag or jar, seal it airtight. Keep it in a cool, dry, dark spot away from the stove and the dishwasher. Moisture causes clumping and flat flavor. A weak aroma or flat taste means the coffee is stale, which is a quality issue. If you see visible mold, smell something musty or sour, or find damp clumps or pantry insects, throw it out.


**Is freeze-dried instant coffee different from spray-dried?**


A little, though both start the same way: as brewed coffee extract. Freeze-drying freezes the extract to about –40°C, cuts it into granules, then dries them at low temperature under vacuum. Spray drying sprays the extract into hot air at the top of a tall tower, and the droplets fall as fine powder.
